# Wintonicz

> Windows support toolbox: one executable with a terminal UI, a command line, and JSON output. Windows 10/11 x64. No telemetry, no installer, no self-update.

Run without installing (PowerShell):
  irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MatheusCampagnolo/wintonicz/main/scripts/run.ps1 | iex
Run a command (arguments need the script-block form):
  & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MatheusCampagnolo/wintonicz/main/scripts/run.ps1))) port find 8080 --json

## Discover what it can do
- `wintonicz tools list --json` lists every tool with id, risk (read, launch, change, destructive), admin (none, optional, required), duration, and CLI command.
- `wintonicz mcp --read-only` is an MCP server (stdio) exposing only the read-only tools; see docs/ai.md.
- `wintonicz tools describe <id> --json` adds the exact command an action would run.

## Rules for agents
- Prefer `--json`. Output is one document: `{schemaVersion, ok, tool, command, data, warnings, error, meta}`. Check `ok` first. Errors are in the same envelope on stdout.
- Read tools never change the system. Actions need `--yes`; without it they print a preview and exit 4. `--dry-run` always previews and exits 0.
- Never pass `--yes` for risk `change` or `destructive` unless the human approved that specific action.
- Destructive tools (`clean ...`, `process end`) list what they will touch in `--dry-run`; show that to the human first.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 needs administrator, 4 not run (preview, declined, read-only), 10 the underlying command failed.
- If `error.code` is `needs_admin`, ask the human; elevation opens a UAC prompt.
- `--read-only` (or `WTZ_READ_ONLY=1`) refuses every action. `WTZ_JSON=1` makes JSON the default.
- Inputs are validated and never passed to a shell. Do not try to work around a rejected value.

More: docs/ai.md
